info.title: Omnikom Platform functions
info.description: Supabase Edge Functions and the per-site form endpoint. User-facing functions take the user's Supabase JWT (bearerAuth, verify_jwt on). Machine-called functions run with verify_jwt = false (supabase/config.toml) and verify their own credential in code first (jobToken, runnerSecret, siteSignature, cronSecret). The database enforces the tenancy wall (02-BACKEND.md). Error bodies use the Problem schema with contract/store codes (07-SPECS.md).

servers.description: projectRef is the Supabase project reference id (not the project name)

mailOutboxSignature.name: X-Cron-Signature
mailOutboxSignature.description:
The mail outbox key (function secret MAIL_OUTBOX_KEY; the same value is in Vault as mail_outbox_key for pg_cron). Header value t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t
METHOD
path?query
body">, accepted for 300 s (supabase/functions/_shared/signature.ts); checked in code (verify_jwt = false)

resendWebhookSignature.name: svix-signature
resendWebhookSignature.description: Resend's webhook signing secret (function secret RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, whsec_ and a base64 key). Resend signs the Svix way: headers svix-id, svix-timestamp and svix-signature; the signed text is <svix-id>.<svix-timestamp>.<raw body>, HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the base64-decoded key, base64 out, the header one or more v1,<signature> separated by spaces; a timestamp more than 300 s off is refused (supabase/functions/mail-events/index.ts); checked in code (verify_jwt = false)

runnerSecret.name: X-Runner-Signature
runnerSecret.description:
Runner key. Header value t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t
METHOD
path?query
body">, accepted for 300 s (supabase/functions/_shared/signature.ts); checked in code (verify_jwt = false). The runner is trusted (ADR 0011)

siteSignature.name: X-Site-Signature
siteSignature.description:
That site's own signing key. Header value t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t
METHOD
path?query
body">, accepted for 300 s (supabase/functions/_shared/signature.ts); checked in code (verify_jwt = false)

cronSignature.name: X-Cron-Signature
cronSignature.description:
The cron key (function secret CRON_KEY; the same value is in Vault as metrics_cron_key for pg_cron). Header value t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t
METHOD
path?query
body">, accepted for 300 s (supabase/functions/_shared/signature.ts); checked in code (verify_jwt = false). Work order 44 replaced the X-Internal-Secret header of the first plan with this one signature scheme

request_id.description: the id of the call: also the x-request-id header and the first word of its log lines

signOff.description: staff only, when a locked field changes

base.description: the version the editor started from. Required when row is set (400 BODY without it); for a new row it is optional and, when sent, must be 0. A save on top of a newer version is refused 409 S-STALE (slice 5.2; service.save_as p_base)

site.description: the site to rebuild (a workspace may have more than one)

versions.description: the version of each row that was validated; the job ships exactly these (dry run 2, N4); required unless preview

preview.description: book row B15: true builds a preview of the saved changes that are ready, at their newest version, to the site's draft address (rows and versions are not read); owners and staff

dispatched.description: false when the build did not reach GitHub (no dispatch token, GitHub refused or unreachable): the job stays queued and the reaper fails it after 24 hours; never a silent success

reason.description: why dispatched is false: no dispatch token, no repository configured, github <status>, github unreachable

left_out.description: book row B15, a preview: the saved changes not in it, each { row, collection, path } (the field the publish-ready wall wants)

PublishResponse.description: a job holding a snapshot of exact versions; nothing goes live until the job is done

processed.description: false until the media processor (build runner) has made sizes and stripped EXIF

Export.description: Everything one publish job needs, as one document (factory/README.md section 1). A rerun of the same job returns the same snapshot and rows. The runner holds the account deploy token itself (02-BACKEND section 8); no token travels in this document.

schema.description: the factory refuses any other value

snapshot.description: { row_id: version } the build ships; a rerun ships the same

id.description: the runner refuses if this differs from client_payload.site_id

contract.description: the resolved site contract (contracts/README.md): the active site_contracts.resolved

gateReport.description: per gate: pass/fail, findings in plain words; at most 64 KiB (413 beyond)

JobCallback.description: state is one of building | gating | deploying | done | failed (a queued or unknown state is 400). The database decides whether the change is legal (409 S-JOB-STATE).

flow.description: Optional. Which journey on the site produced this lead (a hero tab, a calculator, a landing flow). A lower-case slug, not a closed list, because one procedure serves every industry (DECISIONS 3, 14). Real-estate example (ELEV8): home-value, home-finder, sell, cash-offer, contact. Another industry names its own flows. Checking the value against the site contract is UNPROVEN (not built). Different from form, which is the contract form id.

cta.description: Optional. The label of the button or link the visitor used to start the form.

assignee.description: Optional. Slug of the team row the visitor asked for (for example from an agent profile page). The server checks it against that workspace's team rows and ignores an unknown slug (UNPROVEN, not built).

marketingConsent.description: Optional. Consent to marketing messages, kept separate from consentText (permission to contact the visitor about this request). given is false when the box was left empty; text is the exact wording shown next to the box.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Made by the form when it loads and reused on every retry of the same submission, so a retry cannot store the lead twice. Deduplication on the server is UNPROVEN (not built).

status.description: Work order 20: a status key of the business's own list (its contract's crm.statuses, or spam); the database decides (400 I-ANSWER status). One `status` event with from, to, date, who and the author

owner.description: a team row of the workspace; a member cannot hand a lead to someone else (403 S-OWN-ONLY)

note.description: Work order 20: the note carries its author (detail.author { kind: user | agent, name }) as well as the user id and the time of its timeline row

unassign.description: true takes the lead off its owner

read.description: true marks the lead read for the caller (service.mark_lead_read: the lead is bold in their list until they open it), alone or with the other fields; together, both run in one transaction, so a refused change marks nothing. false does nothing (there is no "unread")

fields.description: Work order 01: core fields (name, email, phone, status, owner) and editable industry fields, typed by the contract; answers 200 { changed }

follow_up.description: Work order 18: the lead's follow-up date and time (with an offset, 2026-11-20T10:00:00Z); null clears it; absent leaves it alone. One `follow-up` event with old and new when it changes, in the same transaction as the other changes

status_date.description: Work order 20: the day the status schedules (a status whose list entry has needsDate takes one: 400 I-ANSWER status_date without it); absent keeps the lead's

status_who.description: Work order 20: the member who made the contact (needsWho statuses); absent takes the caller; a person who is not a member of the business is 400 I-ANSWER status_who

status_text.description: Work order 20: one short line the status asks for (needsText), up to 200 characters

LeadUpdateRequest.description: every field but lead is optional; each change writes its own event on the lead timeline (service.lead_update)

consentText.description: the wording the person agreed to, as said or shown; it goes on the consent ledger

owner.description: a team row of the workspace; ignored for a member: their own lead lands on their own team row

processed.description: false until the runner calls media-process-callback

dispatched.description: false when the media job did not reach GitHub (no token, GitHub refused); reason says why

ExportMedia.description: One PROCESSED photo of the workspace (an unprocessed one is left out). `path` is the widest WebP derivative slot that exists (2400 if the original is at least 2400 px wide, else 1600 if at least 1600, else 800, which always exists), never the original upload (the original keeps its GPS data); `url` is a signed download URL for that derivative (1 hour).

path.description: <upload path without extension>-<slot>.webp with slot 2400, 1600 or 800, inside <workspace id>/

original_path.description: storage path of the upload; information only, never signed or served

width.description: of the original after its orientation was applied

url.description: signed download URL for `path`, valid 1 hour; null when Storage would not sign it (then `error` is "sign failed" and the runner fails the build if the file is referenced)

MediaExport.description: Where one uploaded file is and where the runner puts its sizes. Every URL is signed (Storage, secret key) and the secret key never leaves the function.

path.description: storage path of the original upload, <workspace id>/<uuid>.<ext>

url.description: signed download URL of the original, valid 1 hour

uploads.description: signed upload URLs (upsert allowed) for <path without extension>-<width>.webp, in the same workspace folder

MediaProcessCallback.description: The runner reports one processed photo. exifStripped must be the boolean true (422 I-EXIF otherwise: nothing unprocessed is published). A PDF sends only { media, kind: "document" } and is answered 422 I-MEDIA-SIZE: the data model has no document flag yet.

width.description: of the original after its orientation was applied

sizes.description: the widths that were made (accepted, not stored)

skipped.description: widths not made because the original is narrower (accepted, not stored)

newest.description: the newest saved version of the row

published.description: the published version; null for a row never published

drafts.description: newest edit first. Owner and staff see every waiting row, an agent only the rows they could publish themselves; inbox rows and deleted rows never

SettingsSaveRequest.description: one site's lead alerts. Owner or staff. There is no CRM connection any more: leads leave as an export (docs/product/5-crm.md)

site.description: must belong to workspace (404 S-NOT-FOUND otherwise)

to.description: lower-cased and de-duplicated; more than 10 addresses after that, or an address that is not valid, is 422 I-EMAIL

assignee.description: also alert the lead's owner; null or absent keeps the current tick

filter.description: new = status not-contacted (work order 20; it was new); all = every status except spam; mine = assigned to the caller, except spam; spam = spam

q.description: matches name, email and phone, case-insensitive, once it is at least 2 characters; shorter is ignored

template.description: a crm_templates id of the workspace

timezone.description: IANA name; the day the us and eu date forms print

due.description: The view's Due tick (work order 20): only the leads whose follow-up has come or that have an open task due, as lead-list does

duplicates.description: The view's Duplicates tick (work order 20): only the leads flagged as duplicates, as lead-list does

LeadExportRequest.description: Without workspace: site (required), filter, q (block 1's body). With workspace (the CRM view): search, filters, sort, due, duplicates, timezone, and optionally template; with template the file is in that CRM's layout, without it block 1's plain file from the same view.

team_row.description: a team row of this workspace to link the person to

user.description: the login: found by email, or created through the Auth admin API; the sign-in link is never stored, logged or returned

email_sent.description: true when Auth answered 2xx to the mail call (POST /auth/v1/invite for a new login, POST /auth/v1/otp for an existing one); false otherwise (Auth down, its rate limit)

due.description: Work order 18: true keeps the leads whose follow-up date has come or that have an open task whose time has come

duplicates.description: Work order 18: true keeps the flagged leads (a duplicate of an older lead of the business, by email or phone)

rows.description: Each row: id, created_at, name, email, phone, status, owner, form, page, site, follow_up (date-time or null), duplicate (boolean), duplicate_of (the older lead's id, only when the caller may read that lead too, else null), and one key per industry column

value.description: action status: a status key of the business's own list (a status that needs a date is refused: one lead at a time); owner: a team row id or null

field.description: name, email, phone, status, owner, created_at, form, page_path, flow, cta, or answers.<industry key>

transform.description: first | last (name), street | city | state | postal_code (address), e164 | us (phone), iso | us | eu (date)

field.description: name, email, phone, status, owner, created_at, form, page_path, flow, cta, or answers.<industry key>

transform.description: first | last (name), street | city | state | postal_code (address), e164 | us (phone), iso | us | eu (date)

name.description: the team profile's name; null when there is no profile

latest.description: the newest finished job per target whose audit summary is version 1; summary is the whole summary, fails included

history.description: the last 10 finished jobs (done or failed), newest first; summary is null in every row and no fails are carried

target.description: null for a job from before the summary (no version 1)

pass.description: null for a job from before the summary

counts.description: { PASS, FAIL, SKIP } and any other status the audit counted; null for a job from before the summary

truncated.description: how many FAILs were left out of fails

query.description: the shape LeadListRequest takes without the workspace: search, filters, sort (page and size are kept but unused); default {}

columns.description: the list's column keys in order: core keys, industry columns, follow_up, duplicate

shared.description: true: a view for the whole business (owner or staff with MFA). Default false

LeadTaskRequest.description: Exactly one shape: { lead, text, due? } adds, { task, done } marks

done.description: true finishes the task, false reopens it

Refused.description: refused by a wall (S-ROLE, S-OWN-ONLY, S-LOCKED, S-SIGNOFF)

NotFound.description: not found (also any row of another workspace)

Conflict.description: S-SINGLETON: there is already one; edit it. S-STALE (save): the row was saved at a newer version by someone else; the message names the row id and the newest version

MethodNotAllowed.description: METHOD: only POST (a browser preflight OPTIONS is answered 204 before anything else)

TooLarge.description: SIZE: the body is over 256 KiB

ServerError.description: SERVER or CONFIG: something went wrong on our side; the answer says nothing about the cause

post.summary: Save a draft version (FR-4, FR-6, FR-7)

200.description: version saved; the site is unchanged

400.description: BODY: the body is not a SaveRequest (a missing or negative base, a bad id, a field of the wrong type), with the field problems

404.description: not a member of that workspace: returned before any validation, so no field names or limits are revealed (dry run 2, N1)

post.summary: Publish rows and start a build of that site only (FR-8, FR-9)

409.description: a build of this site is running; this one is queued behind it; or S-LIMIT (a Problem): the workspace reached its limit of publishes today

post.summary: Signed upload URL under the workspace prefix (FR-12)

200.description: upload URL

409.description: S-LIMIT: the workspace reached its limit of MB of photos and files

post.summary: Record the upload and the rights tick, queue processing in the runner (FR-12)

200.description: media recorded; processed = false until the runner finishes

get.summary: Freeze and return one job's snapshot, the contract, the rows, the processed media with signed URLs and the site's deploy target (slice 4.3)

200.description: export

409.description: S-JOB-BUSY: another build of this site is running; the runner's queue retries later

get.description: The first call moves the job queued -> building and freezes the snapshot; a rerun returns the same snapshot and changes nothing. Media: processed files only; `path` is the widest derivative slot that exists (2400, 1600 or 800), `url` signs that path (1 hour, at most 8 signed at a time), `original_path` is information only.

get.summary: The runner's media job asks where one uploaded file is and where to put its sizes

200.description: signed download URL of the original and signed upload URLs of the three WebP sizes

502.description: STORAGE: a file could not be signed (it was never uploaded, or Storage is down); the runner retries

post.summary: Runner reports job state and gate report

413.description: the gate report is larger than 64 KiB

post.summary: Called by a site's /api/lead with the site id (FR-13); no user login

parameters.name: visitor
parameters.description: The visitor: sha256 of "<site id>:<visitor address>", put in the signed path by the site's /api/lead (product row E5). Absent or not 64 lower-case hex means no visitor limit for the post and a stored address hash of null.

409.description: The site is paused or its workspace is suspended (code S-SITE-PAUSED or S-WORKSPACE-SUSPENDED): nothing is stored; the site shows the call-us message (step 3, migrations 7 and 8).

429.description: rate limited (per IP and site) Also code S-QUOTA: the workspace reached its hourly lead limit (workspace_limits over platform_limits leads_per_hour_workspace), or one visitor of the site reached its hourly lead limit (leads_per_hour_visitor, 5 by default; product row E5).

post.summary: Send the queued new-lead alerts (pg_cron every minute through service.mail_outbox_tick; product row E4, migration 29)
post.description: Body {}. Claims at most 10 due rows of mail_outbox (service.outbox_claim records each message; a capped one waits for the next day, a suppressed address is dropped) and posts each to Resend, one at a time, with a 10 s timeout and the message id as Resend's idempotency key; service.outbox_done records the answer (a failed try is retried later, the sixth fails the message).

200.description: { claimed, sent, failed }: the rows claimed and how many Resend accepted or not

post.summary: Resend's webhook for a bounced or complained email (product row E21, migration 31)
post.description: Body: Resend's event. A permanent bounce (email.bounced, bounce type Permanent) suppresses the address the email was sent to for the whole platform; a complaint (email.complained) suppresses it for the workspace of the message (service.mail_event: the address comes from our own message that data.email_id names, never from the payload). Any other signed event is answered 200 { handled: false } so Resend does not send it again.

200.description: { handled: false } for an event that is no permanent bounce or complaint, else { handled: true, suppressed } with suppressed 1 for an email id of ours and 0 for none

post.summary: Runner reports processed media (sizes, EXIF stripped)

422.description: I-EXIF: exifStripped was not true; I-MEDIA-SIZE: a document, or a width or height below 1 (the file stays unprocessed)

post.summary: Pull one workspace's search numbers into metrics_snapshots (pg_cron, 03:30 UTC, two calls per workspace; work order 44)
post.description: Body {}. The site measured is the workspace's live site, else its oldest preview one. Without `source`: search-console (always a BLOCKED row until a property is verified) and bing. With source=pagespeed: PageSpeed on five pages plus CrUX, weekly (a call on a day it is not due answers `skipped`). A source that cannot be read is a BLOCKED row (data.blocked), never a guess; one that throws is under `failed` and writes no row. 502 when nothing was written and something failed. 404 for a workspace that is not trial or active.

200.description: { workspace, day, site: { id, state, origin }, written: [{ source, blocked }], skipped: [text], failed: [{ source, error }], notes: [text] }

post.summary: Tell the search engines a live site's sitemap changed (job-callback runs the same code on done of a production job; work order 44)
post.description: Body {}. For the site of the job: Search Console submit (BLOCKED until a property is verified) and an IndexNow ping of the sitemap's addresses, sent only when the site hosts a key file (none does yet, work order 45), appended to the day's bing row. { skipped } for a site that is not live; 404 for a job that does not exist.

200.description: { skipped } or { sitemap, searchConsole: { ok, status?, blocked? }, indexnow: { sent, reason?, status?, urls? } }

post.summary: Delete an item: soft delete, off the site with the next publish, its versions kept (owner/staff; supabase/functions/unpublish)
Change a lead: status, owner, a note, or unassign (dashboard; supabase/functions/lead-update)

204.description: done; each change is on the lead timeline

400.description: the body is not a LeadUpdateRequest

404.description: no such lead, or one the caller cannot see (another workspace's lead, a member's colleague's lead): the same answer

post.summary: Add a lead by hand (dashboard; supabase/functions/add-lead)

201.description: lead created; the consent wording is on the consent ledger

400.description: the body is not an AddLeadRequest (bad email, no consent wording, too long)

404.description: no such site, or the caller is not a member of its workspace

post.summary: The rows with changes waiting to be published, for "Publish N changes" (dashboard, read-only; supabase/functions/drafts)

200.description: the waiting rows, newest edit first

400.description: BODY: site is missing or not an id

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: no such site, or one the caller cannot see

post.summary: Save the lead alerts from Settings (dashboard; owner or staff; supabase/functions/settings-save)

200.description: saved. The screen reads the new values back through RLS

400.description: BODY: no alerts (a crm key is ignored beside alerts and is not a request on its own), a bad id, or a list of the wrong type

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: the caller is not an owner of the workspace or staff, or the site is not in this workspace (an agent gets this too)

422.description: I-EMAIL: an address is not valid, or more than ten remain after de-duplication

post.summary: Export the leads under the current filter as a CSV file (dashboard; supabase/functions/lead-export)
post.description: The leads are read as the caller under Row Level Security: owner and staff get every lead of the site, an agent only the leads assigned to them. Newest first, at most 5000. Cells that start with = + - @ get a leading quote. One `exported` event is written per lead in the file. A body with `workspace` (work orders 02 and 07) is { workspace, template?, search?, filters?, sort?, timezone? }: the leads of the caller's CRM view (service.lead_list: the same search, filters and sort, exactly what RLS shows the caller; a workspace the caller cannot see is 404), at most 5000 (X-Omnikom-Export-Capped), one `exported` event per lead. With `template` they come in the map's columns and order, phones and dates in the client's form, value maps applied, industry columns included, the formula guard on every cell. Without `template` the file is this same plain file (the columns below), written from the view. A `template` without `workspace` is a 400.

200.description: the file: columns received (UTC ISO), name, email, phone, form, page, status, owner, answers (one JSON cell)

X-Omnikom-Export-Capped.description: 5000, present only when there were more leads than that; the file holds the newest 5000

400.description: BODY: site is missing or not an id, filter is not one of new, all, mine, spam

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: no such site, or one the caller cannot see: no file

post.summary: Invite a person to the workspace (dashboard; owner or staff; supabase/functions/invite-member)
post.description: Finds the login with this email or creates it through the Auth admin API (no email is sent by that call), makes the person a member, then asks Auth to send the mail: a new login gets the invite mail (who invited them and to which business, from the user data), a login that already existed and is confirmed gets the sign-in link mail, and one that never opened its invite gets the invite again, its user data set to this business and inviter first. email_sent is Auth's own answer; a mail that did not go does not undo the membership. Inviting the same address again finds the same login.

200.description: they are a member; email_sent says whether Auth sent the mail

400.description: BODY: a missing field, an email that is not valid, a role that is not owner or member

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: the caller is not an owner of the workspace or staff with MFA, or the team row is not one of this workspace's (an agent gets this too, and no login is created)

409.description: S-LAST-OWNER: an owner cannot demote themselves while they are the last one

502.description: AUTH: the Auth admin API did not create the login; try again

post.summary: The members of the workspace for the People card (dashboard; owner or staff; supabase/functions/team-list)

200.description: every member, owners first

400.description: BODY: no workspace, or one that is not an id

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: the caller is not an owner of the workspace or staff with MFA, or the workspace does not exist (an agent gets this too)

post.summary: Remove a person from the workspace (dashboard; owner or staff; supabase/functions/member-remove)
post.description: service.remove_member: never the last owner; one audit row; the person's leads, edits and uploads stay. Their open sessions are not ended (Supabase Auth has no admin logout by user id); every request is checked against membership, so their next request in this workspace is refused.

200.description: removed

400.description: BODY: no workspace or user, or one that is not an id

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: the caller is not an owner of the workspace or staff with MFA, or the person is not a member of it (an agent gets this too)

409.description: S-LAST-OWNER: a workspace keeps at least one owner

post.summary: The CRM lead list on the server: search, filter, sort and page (dashboard; supabase/functions/lead-list)
post.description: Exactly the leads the caller may read (owner and staff: the workspace; a member: its own; anyone else: none, and no field names). Sort and filter keys are the core columns (created_at, name, email, phone, status, owner, form, page, site: the site's id, work order 07) and the contract's industry columns; a number field sorts as a number; empty values last, then newest first. At most 200 a page. Columns come as an array in contract form order; each row carries each column under its own key, typed.

200.description: The page, the total and the columns

400.description: BODY: site is missing or not an id, filter is not one of new, all, mine, spam

422.description: S-QUERY: a sort or filter key that is not a column, a bad filter, or a page of more than 200

post.summary: Set status or owner of, or delete, many leads at once (dashboard; supabase/functions/leads-bulk)
post.description: All or nothing: an id the caller may not act on refuses the whole call (404) and writes nothing. Owner and delete are for an owner (403 S-OWN-ONLY). Delete is the hard delete and needs confirm: true (409 S-CONFIRM); one audit row per deleted lead, the consent ledger kept. A single delete is a bulk of one.

200.description: How many leads changed or were deleted

400.description: BODY: site is missing or not an id, filter is not one of new, all, mine, spam

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: an id the caller may not act on

post.summary: Propose how the columns of the client's CRM file map to our lead fields (dashboard; supabase/functions/crm-map-propose)
post.description: Owner only (a member 403 S-OWN-ONLY, anyone else 404). Our fields are the core lead fields and the workspace's industry fields in form order. Send the headers and at most 20 sample rows, or the file (at most 1 MB; its first 20 rows are the samples). A pair under 0.5 is never assigned. Stores nothing.

200.description: The proposed map, a score per pair, what was left unmapped and the warnings

400.description: BODY: a field is missing or not valid

post.summary: Confirm and save a map of the client's CRM layout (dashboard; supabase/functions/crm-template-save)
post.description: Owner only. The map is checked by tools/crm-map (validateTemplate, every transform known) and every industry field it names must be on this business's forms; the database checks the same. One map per workspace and name: saving a name again updates that row.

200.description: The map's id

400.description: BODY: a field is missing or not valid

409.description: T-NAME: another map has that name

422.description: T-COLUMNS, T-TRANSFORM, T-FIELD (naming the field): the map is not valid

post.summary: Import the client's own CRM file through a saved map; a dry run first (dashboard; supabase/functions/lead-import)
post.description: Owner only. The file (CSV, at most 1 MB and 5000 rows, work order 02 F6; a bigger file is refused whole before it is parsed, 413 I-FILE or I-ROWS) is parsed and mapped with tools/crm-map, then every row is typed as a capture is, and duplicates (same email, any case, or same phone in E.164, against the workspace and the file) are found. A dry run (the default) writes nothing and reports the first 20 rows as they would be stored. A real run (dry_run false) needs consent true (the owner's tick "These people agreed to be contacted by my business") and duplicates skip or add; it is all or nothing; each lead gets form import, that sentence with the date and the file's name as its consent text, one received event and one consent ledger row; one audit row holds the file's sha256 and the counts.

200.description: The dry run's report, or the real run's counts

400.description: BODY: a field is missing or not valid

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: the map is not this workspace's

413.description: I-ROWS: more rows than the cap (the answer says how many)

422.description: I-CONSENT, I-DUPLICATES, I-IMPORT (the line and the field of the first bad row; nothing imported), T-FIELD (the map names a field the forms no longer have)

post.summary: A site's stored search check: the latest audit summary per target and the last 10 publishes (dashboard; supabase/functions/site-audit)
post.description: Read back from the site's publish jobs (every publish stores its audit summary, tools/audit/summary.mjs version 1, in the job's gate report). Owner of the site's workspace, or staff with MFA; a member, another workspace's owner and a site that does not exist all get 404, as site settings are hidden from members. latest.<target> is the newest finished job of that target whose summary is version 1 (the summary whole, fails included), or null; history is the last 10 finished jobs (done or failed) newest first, each without fails; a job from before the summary has pass and counts null and never appears in latest.

200.description: The latest summary per target and the history

400.description: BODY: site is missing or not an id

post.summary: Save a CRM view: a lead-list query plus an ordered column list (dashboard; supabase/functions/view-save)
post.description: Migration 22 service.view_save. A member saves their own views; shared: true (a view for the whole business) is for an owner or staff with the second factor (403 S-OWN-ONLY). The query is checked by the very code lead-list uses (422 S-QUERY: a saved view can never hold a query lead-list refuses); every column key must be a column of the list (400 I-ANSWER on `columns`, naming the key; follow_up and duplicate are columns too). With `id` the view is changed in place; another person's private view, another workspace's view and an unknown id are 404 S-NOT-FOUND. A name is 1 to 60 characters, unique per person (and among the shared views): 400 I-ANSWER on `name`. At most 100 views per person and workspace. Views are listed by the dashboard with a plain select (row level security: your own and the shared ones), not by a function.

200.description: The id of the saved view

400.description: BODY: a field is missing or not valid; I-ANSWER: a name, column or limit the database refused, with the words in problems

403.description: S-OWN-ONLY: a member shares a view or changes a shared one

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: not a member of the workspace, or a view that is not the caller's to change

422.description: S-QUERY: a query lead-list would refuse

post.summary: Delete a saved CRM view (dashboard; supabase/functions/view-delete)
post.description: Migration 22 service.view_delete. The caller's own view, or a shared view for an owner (a member 403 S-OWN-ONLY). Another person's private view, another workspace's view and an unknown id are 404 S-NOT-FOUND.

400.description: BODY: view is missing or not an id

403.description: S-OWN-ONLY: a member deletes a shared view

post.summary: Add a task to a lead, or finish or reopen one (dashboard; supabase/functions/lead-task)
post.description: Migration 22 service.task_add / service.task_done. Send { lead, text, due? } to add (201) or { task, done } to mark (200); both shapes or neither is 400. The lead must be one the caller may act on (an owner: any; a member: leads assigned to them), else 404 S-NOT-FOUND, also for another workspace. A task is read exactly where its lead is (row level security). Each change writes a `task` event (added, done, reopened) on the lead timeline; asking for the state a task is already in writes none. A lead keeps at most 100 tasks.

200.description: The task was finished or reopened

400.description: BODY: not exactly one shape, a text of 0 or over 500 characters, due not a date and time with an offset, done not a yes or no

404.description: S-NOT-FOUND: a lead or task the caller may not act on
